summary:
The round-one and round-two machine reports both passed with no errors. An independent rerun on the current JSON files also passed. Logistics JSON and Markdown agree on welcome and check-in (16:00–16:25), icebreaker (16:25–16:45), career panel (16:45–17:30), structured networking (17:30–18:15), refreshment break (18:15–18:40), and closing (18:40–19:00). The six blocks are continuous in local time and the occupied staffing cells match the JSON volunteer lists, using V1–V6. Accessibility covers a checked step-free route and restroom, admission hold with an acting lead, integrated seating and clear aisles, accommodation requests, large-print and plain-text materials, spoken and written updates, quiet seating, flexible participation and seated refreshment delivery. The contingency table names triggers, actions and owners for AV or Wi-Fi failure, speaker absence, volunteer absence and stock shortages. V6 directs attendees to printed materials on AV failure, and V3 uses facilitated peer discussion if no speakers are available. For simultaneous V1 and V5 absences known before doors open, V6 covers check-in with self-service tags and gives seat directions until V2 takes over. V3 handles the welcome and can receive late speakers. During networking V6 calls rounds and holds release for V2's label checks. During service V3 handles announcements and replenishment, V2 runs the combined station and tracks first servings, V4 handles seated requests, and V6 manages the queue. The findings identify an opening handoff gap if the absences overlap after admission starts and a conflicting budget reference.

The six unique Budget r2 SKUs match the catalog prices, Budget Markdown and Logistics supply table. SNACK10 provides 30 servings (3 × 10) for 4200 cents, FRUIT10 provides 30 (3 × 10) for 3000, WATER24 provides 72 (3 × 24) for 2400, TAG25 provides 75 (3 × 25) for 1350, MARKER4 provides eight (2 × 4) for 700, and PRINT25 provides 75 copies (3 × 25) for 1950. The plan covers 60 food servings, 72 drinks and 75 tags for 50 attendees. Purchases total 13600 cents. The 16400-cent reserve exceeds the 3000-cent minimum and the total is 30000 cents at the cap. Both plans agree on free venue and equipment, eight shared markers, and 50 agendas plus 25 copies for signs or backups. Budget flags the double-sided and mixed-use print assumptions for confirmation. For a remaining deficit after release of usable surplus (planned 10 food and 22 drinks), Budget r2 rounds food deficit ÷ 10 and drink deficit ÷ 24 separately up to whole packs at 1000 and 800 cents respectively. The cumulative 13400-cent draw limit leaves at least 3000 cents in reserve. Replacing one snack pack with one fruit pack would preserve food coverage and save 400 cents, giving 13200 cents in purchases and 16800 in reserve if adopted.

Instagram, flyer and promotional email each stand alone with Women in Tech: Connect & Grow, Friday, February 19, 2027, 16:00–19:00 local time, room for 50 college students, all six matching activities and times, and [Venue], [RSVP link] and [Accessibility contact]. The flyer and email use [Speaker names]. Instagram identifies no speakers by name. The participation options match Logistics r2, and the flyer and email promises of one food and one drink per attendee are supported by Budget r2.

findings.evidence: outputs/demo-02/logistics-r2/logistics.md, If V1 is absent, assigns V2 check-in through 16:22 and assigns V6 to cover when V2 is still counting at opening. If V5 is absent, Departure before service sends V2 away at the first pause in the current block to verify the tally and stage stock, with self-service tags for arrivals. If V1 is already absent and V5 leaves after doors open but before 16:22, the combined-absence check-in instruction does not cover V2 stepping away. V6's ordinary welcome duty is seating and V3 is receiving speakers.
findings.impact: A mid-opening stock handoff can leave the active check-in post uncovered while arrivals still need check-in and agendas. The same combined schedule gives V6 the speaker briefing with no specified transfer deadline if the check-in overlap runs into the icebreaker.
findings.request: Apply the combined-absence coverage whenever V2 must leave check-in for refreshment duties before 16:22, including a V5 departure after doors open. Name the check-in owner and how the transfer is signaled, or explicitly defer V2’s stock work to a named time. Specify who briefs and stages speakers by 16:42 if V6 is still occupied with arrivals.

findings.evidence: outputs/demo-02/logistics-r2/logistics.md, Budget handoff, directs volunteers to reconcile shortage owners with Budget revision 1. The shortage bullet in outputs/demo-02/budget-r1/budget.md names V5 and V1 only. The current procedure in outputs/demo-02/budget-r2/budget.md, steps 1–4, explicitly gives V2 the station and shortage response if V5 is absent and V3 the replenishment decision if V1 is absent.
findings.impact: Following the cited version during an absence can send a deficit to the absent lead or obscure who has purchasing authority, delaying a time-sensitive order.
findings.request: Point the operational handoff to Budget r2’s Refreshment shortage procedure and make that current reference explicit alongside the V2-to-V3 escalation.

verified.evidence: In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r1/logistics.md, the volunteer-absence contingency moved V2 to a combined station during the break while the shortage row still assigned V5. The shortage bullet in outputs/demo-02/budget-r1/budget.md also assumed V5 counted stock and alerted V1. In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r2/logistics.md, If V5 is absent assigns V2 pre-opening count and separate staging, pre-service rechecks with duties handed off or handled using printed prompts, and both food labeling and drink-label checks before V6 releases attendees. For a departure during service V6 pauses the queue, V2 reconciles servings already distributed against usable stock, consolidates and relabel-checks the station, and clears V6 to restart. V2 tracks first food and drink servings and V4 continues seated delivery. The revised shortage row and outputs/demo-02/budget-r2/budget.md steps 1–4 agree on usable surplus, recount, holding seconds, prioritizing outstanding first servings including seated requests, and immediate item-level escalation from V2 to V1 or acting lead V3.

In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r1/logistics.md, the Volunteer assignments table included V1's check-in, welcome, icebreaker and closing duties, while the absence contingency only shifted coordination and transition cues to V3. In outputs/demo-02/logistics-r2/logistics.md, If V1 is absent now assigns V2 check-in and tags through 16:22, V3 speaker reception before the welcome and start cue, then V3 icebreaker leadership and wrap-up while V6 briefs and positions speakers. V3 announces the panel format and times segments while moderating, with V6 on AV and networking instructions. V6 calls networking rounds and staggers release. V3 owns the refreshment rule, replenishment decision and 18:35 cue, and leads reflection, concludes sharing, reads the recap and dismisses by 19:00. The current-block takeover and cue rule cover mid-event V1 departure. Budget r2 step 3 independently confirms V3's authority. The combined mid-opening scenario is recorded as a separate finding.
